slides.title: Your booking confirmation, decoded
slides.sub: 6 lines to check before you travel.

slides.title: The confirmation number.
slides.body: Keep it handy offline. It's the first thing reception or support will ask for.

slides.title: The guest name.
slides.body: It should match the ID of the person checking in. Typos are easy to fix early.

slides.title: Dates and number of nights.
slides.body: Check-in and check-out days, not just the month. Late-night bookings slip a day easily.

slides.title: Room type and board.
slides.body: Twin or double bed, room only or breakfast included. It should match what you chose.

slides.title: The cancellation deadline.
slides.body: Note the exact date and time. After it, the free cancellation usually ends.

slides.title: What's still due at the hotel.
slides.body: Some local taxes are paid on arrival. Your booking details say if anything is left to pay.

slides.title: Something looks wrong?
slides.body: Our support team answers 7 days a week.

caption:
Most hotel problems start with a booking nobody read twice.

Check the confirmation number, the guest name, the dates, the room and board, the cancellation deadline and anything still to pay at the hotel. Two minutes, done.

slides.kicker: Save this for your family trip
slides.title: Booking a hotel with kids? Check these 6 things
slides.sub: Fewer surprises at the front desk.

slides.title: Enter every guest, with ages.
slides.body: Children often count towards room capacity. The right search shows rooms that really fit.

slides.title: Count the beds, not the guests.
slides.body: A room for four can mean one double and a sofa bed. Read the bed setup.

slides.title: Ask for a cot in advance.
slides.body: Hotels usually have a limited number. Add it to your special requests.

slides.title: Check the extra bed policy.
slides.body: Some hotels charge per night for an extra bed or a child. Look before you book.

slides.title: Two rooms can beat one big room.
slides.body: Compare the price of two standard rooms with a family room. Ask for connecting ones.

slides.title: Look at what's around.
slides.body: A park, a supermarket and a short walk to transport matter more with kids.

slides.title: Amsterdam: where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 neighbourhoods, 5 very different trips.

slides.title: Canal Ring
slides.body: The classic canals, gabled houses and most sights within walking distance.

slides.title: Jordaan
slides.body: Quiet canals, brown cafés, small galleries and weekend markets.

slides.title: De Pijp
slides.body: The Albert Cuyp Market, lively terraces and cafés from every corner of the world.

slides.title: Museum Quarter
slides.body: The Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum and Vondelpark nearby.

slides.title: Amsterdam Noord
slides.body: Across the IJ by free ferry. Old shipyards, street art and waterfront spots.

slides.title: Early flight in, late flight out
slides.sub: How to handle the hours outside check-in.

slides.title: Leave your bags at the hotel.
slides.body: Most hotels will store luggage before check-in and after check-out. Just ask.

slides.title: Ask for early check-in when you book.
slides.body: Add it to your special requests. It's never guaranteed, but it helps the hotel plan.

slides.title: Landing at dawn? Book the night before.
slides.body: One extra night means a room is ready the moment you arrive. Compare the cost.

slides.title: Pack a small day bag on top.
slides.body: Charger, toothbrush and a change of clothes, so the big case can stay locked away.

slides.title: Plan an easy first and last day.
slides.body: Choose sights close to the hotel, so picking up your bags takes minutes, not an hour.
